sourceCounts.source: games/chronoforge/src/world.js, ported in Phase 1.2 to docs/specs/world-graph.mjs. Interiors carry worldDrop null and zero encounters. doorwayEdges counts doorway RECORDS (20 outdoor directed doors over 10 bidirectional region edges, plus 4 interior exits); the donor's 18 was 14 + 4 over 7 edges. level accepted 3 lateral cycles in Phase 1.2 — per-tier reachability is unchanged at 4/6/8/8.

coreSeams.what: Read-only getter exposing ctx, for tools that must build a scene rather than photograph one.

openIssues.text: No ambient occlusion or contact shadow. Small props read as pasted on when they stand inside a cast shadow. This is half of defect 3 and it needs an AO pass in Tier 1.
Depth of field is not implemented. It needs a DepthTexture, which cannot share the 4x MSAA scene target; add a resolved depth prepass in Tier 1. Do not bolt DOF onto the current target.
Ground detail normal map repeats visibly at its ~22 m tile from the top shot. Needs a second octave at a different repeat, or triplanar variation.
The placeholder heightfield reads as sand dunes: ridged noise plus a bright sandy palette. It is scaffolding, not a look decision, and Tier 1 replaces it.
Night lighting was tuned to a readable linear median of 0.03 but has had no art pass. Tier 1 owns it.
FRAME_HEIGHT_M = 18 (the deferred orthographic scale) is set from a pixel-height argument, not from playtesting a party of three plus enemies. Revisit once traversal lands.

openIssues.title: Dev panel is default-hidden because auto-hide during shots does not work
openIssues.detail: An auto-hide keyed on __DAWN__.shot was tried and failed — the panel update runs before applyShot, so the capture still contains the overlay. Panel is default-off; open with ?dev=1. Needs a correct fix in Tier 5.
openIssues.repro: set visible default true, then: node tools/shot.mjs --shots hero

openIssues.title: 18.7-19.3h reads 0.25-0.31 on wide, just over the ceiling
openIssues.detail: At the SAME sun elevation the evening ground is 1.3-1.4x brighter than the morning ground, measured on `top` which has no sky in frame (elev 18.2: am raw 0.3185 / pm 0.4127; elev 14.6: 0.2256 / 0.3170). Cause is terrain azimuth - the probe region's dune slopes face the setting azimuth 264deg more squarely than the rising 96deg. Cannot be closed by an elevation-keyed ramp; that would need metering, which is rejected by design. Bright, not blown: white% 0.01.

openIssues.title: Noon wide shot washes out at distance; hero shot is correct
openIssues.detail: h12/hero exposes correctly - shadows, metal, dielectric and rock all read. h12/wide goes milky in the far field.
openIssues.cause: horizonColor lerps to pale blue 0x9db9dd as warm -> 0 at density 0.0011, and the grade (contrast 1.06, saturation 1.10, split 0.85) is dawn-tuned. Both are outside the exposure spot-fix and were deliberately not touched.

openIssues.title: Sky is pure black above the horizon during twilight
openIssues.detail: Terrain now reads at 20.0h and 5.2h but the sky mesh is still on night parameters and renders flat black. Real civil twilight has a strong vertical gradient. Opened shots/phase0.1/h20/wide.png and h5/wide.png to confirm.

openIssues.title: Twilight is heavily magenta/violet
openIssues.detail: TWILIGHT_WARM at 0.45 blend. Reads as a deliberate look but is unvalidated against the game palette. One constant in src/render/environment.js.

openIssues.title: 5.1h wide median 0.062 is under the 0.09 band floor
openIssues.detail: 15x better than the 0.004 it was, and the cliff is gone. Sun is at -4.93 deg there vs -2.20 deg at 20.0h, so it is legitimately deeper in twilight. Floor may be the wrong target mid-crossing. Human eyeballed and accepted.

openIssues.title: research_lab tier gate is circular — Ascendant is unreachable in the donor
openIssues.detail: base.js: research_lab tierGate[1]='Ascendant' but Ascendant requires researchBuilt:true. Verified in source. Blocks Transcendent and the win condition. Must be broken when settlement ships.

openIssues.detail: Absent from the starting kit (confirmed against shots/proto-ref/menu-inventory.png, which shows exactly 5 items), every enemy drop table and every world drop. gamedesign added them as 6% secondary drops on Drone Sentinel / Glacier Wolf so the Phase 8 census gate can pass.

openIssues.detail: Escape from the action menu just reopens the same hero next tick. gamedesign proposes a Wait root option plus an arbiter fix; flagged for battle to implement, not applied in Phase 1.1.

openIssues.title: Haventide -> Emberline doorway lands five tiles off its return door
openIssues.detail: games/chronoforge/src/world.js:82 — { x: 44, y: 15, to: { mapId: 'emberline_region', x: 1, y: 20 } }. Emberline's reciprocal door is at (1,15). The other six inherited edges all land exactly on the reciprocal door. Verified in source. Fixed in docs/specs/world-graph.mjs (landing -> (1,15)); selfCheck() now asserts round-trip symmetry on every outdoor edge.

openIssues.title: Haventide interior exit lands on build plot slotIdx 7
openIssues.detail: games/chronoforge/src/world.js:267 — { x: 15, y: 19, to: { mapId: 'haventide_region', x: 12, y: 24 } }. (12,24) is plot slotIdx 7, so once that plot is built the party exits the city inside a building. Verified in source. Landing moved to (12,22) — still south of the city tile so [C] does not re-trigger, clear of all 17 plots. selfCheck() asserts no landing sits on a city tile, plot, encounter or world drop.

openIssues.title: Snow biomes are 1.5-1.6x brighter than the ground the dawn ramp was signed off on
openIssues.detail: frozen_ruins mid albedo 0.448 and frost_canyon 0.398 linear luminance vs grassland_ruins 0.274 (docs/specs/heightfields.mjs prints all eight). The signed-off dawn frame — wide median 0.212, p90 0.51, 0% white — was measured on the Phase 0 placeholder whose ground is 0x9d8259, about 0.26. EXPOSURE_RAMP is fixed per hour with no metering by design, so Orbital Reach and Frost Canyon will read brighter than that baseline and may push p90 toward the 1.2 ceiling. Snow is already dirtied far below its 0.7-0.8 physical albedo to hold the eight-biome spread to 3.96x; level cannot close this further without making snow look like mud. render needs a per-biome albedo trim or a per-biome offset in EXPOSURE_RAMP. Check: probe() on wide at 6.4 h in both snow regions, whitePct must stay < 2.

openIssues.title: crater_ember is the darkest ground in the game at 0.113 luminance
openIssues.detail: Basalt is genuinely 6-8% reflectance and that is the Phase 0 trap in the other direction — a dark ground blows the sky trying to expose it. Mitigated by authoring the mid as ash-grey 0x655d59 rather than basalt black, with the lava emissive supplying the contrast. Still the low end of the 3.96x spread; worth a probe when Crater Ember first renders in Phase 10.

openIssues.title: alien_terraform terracing may read as banding rather than grown platforms
openIssues.detail: The only biome whose landform is not erosional. carve.mix 0.45 at 1.4 m steps with blendFrac 0.90 — a partial quantise, deliberately weak because a full one both bands the surface and multiplies every local gradient by ~1.5/blendFrac. This is the one look decision in the heightfield spec that is not measurable offline. If it reads as banding when Last Crown renders, drop carve.mix toward 0.30.

openIssues.title: Four inherited encounters sit on a landform and want re-placing
openIssues.detail: docs/specs/heightfields.mjs prints local relief within 7 m of all 36 inherited encounter tiles. e17 (6.6 m) and e18 (5.8 m) are on the Frost Canyon trench wall; e35 (4.5 m) is on a Crater Ember rim; e36 (2.5 m) is borderline on a crater lip. The other 32 sit on 0.2-2.6 m and are fine. Phase 1.3 input — encounter data was carried through the port untouched.

openIssues.title: Frost Canyon doorway moved from (30,28) to (23,28) — landform, not a donor bug
openIssues.detail: The frost_canyon heightfield cuts a 47 m trench down the middle of the map and tile (30,28) lands mid-wall at 29.5 deg, over the 20 deg doorway limit. (23,28) is the canyon mouth: trench floor, 3.6 deg. You now enter Frost Canyon by walking up the ravine. Orbital Reach's landing coord moved with it so the edge stays symmetric. Recorded in world-graph.mjs MOVED_FROM_DONOR.

openIssues.title: CORE-CHANGE REQUEST: ridge2D in src/core/rng.js is C0, not C1 — it creases along every ridge crest
openIssues.detail: ridge2D folds with `1 - Math.abs(noise2D(...)*2 - 1)`. An absolute value is C0: the slope flips sign across the fold, so any surface built on it changes gradient discontinuously along EVERY ridge crest. Squaring the result does not repair it — the fold sits at n=1, where d(n^2)/dn = 2. Measured on the bare function, |d2|/e2 grows 1.91x when the probe spacing halves, against 0.0 for noise2D and fbm2D, which are both clean. Six of the eight biomes use a ridge term and every one was creased before this pass. NOT CHANGED — src/core/rng.js is shared core. docs/specs/heightfields.mjs ships a local `ridgeC1` with a hyperbolic fold softened over 12% of the range (same octave structure, same seed stride, same n(0)=1 / n(+/-1)=0 output range) and the integrator should decide whether core adopts it. Also affects src/world/index.js, which uses ridge2D for both the placeholder terrain and makeRock().

openIssues.title: Surface-continuity gate added to heightfields.mjs; six carve defects fixed
openIssues.detail: Max slope is a first-derivative test and structurally cannot see a crease. New gate probes |d2h|/e2 at the 0.5 m mesh spacing and again at 0.25 m: a C1 break doubles, genuine curvature is bounded, so divergence is ~2.0 at a crease and ~1.0 otherwise. Ceiling 1.45. Against the code committed at 2cfc6fa the gate fails 8/8 biomes (grassland 1.97x at exactly x=32=carve.startM, alien 2.71x, neon 2.15x); after the fix the worst is 1.23x. Six defects fixed: shore delta corner; trench lipMix C0 at floor edge AND rim (0.29 slope jump each); crater linear wall + sin() lip; clamp01 corners in the influence masks of five carve kinds; basin/crater winner-takes-all seams (basins now blend with a polynomial smin, craters now SUM compactly-supported C1 bowls so there is no selection); and ridge2D (LVL-5). Two non-crease findings: the damping mask was the largest single gradient in the spec (a 4 m taper on a +/-4 m field contributes 1.12 to the gradient — crater_ember peaked 2.3 m OUTSIDE any crater footprint), now budgeted as INFL_TAPER_M = 12; and crater placement was degenerate, all four centres inside a 10 m cluster at the map middle, now authored as fractional sites with a floors-disjoint assertion.

openIssues.title: PROPOSAL, not implemented: blend biome albedo near doorways
openIssues.detail: The twelve maps are discrete and joined at authored doorway coordinates, so no continuous blend field is needed — only the ground near a door needs to resemble what is through it. Within R metres of a doorway (suggest R = 14 m, a little under half a screen width, lerped on smooth01(1 - d/R)), lerp the biome's four-colour albedo ramp toward the ramp of the map that door leads to. Everything required is already data: doorway coords and target mapId in world-graph.mjs, biome per map, and the four-colour ramp per biome in heightfields.mjs. Scope is three doors, not a system: six of the ten edges already read as natural gradients. The jarring ones are emberline<->forest_veil (0.264 -> 0.170 luminance), emberline<->orbital_reach (0.264 -> 0.448) and mire_bog<->orbital_reach (0.120 -> 0.448, a 3.7x jump). crater_ember<->frost_canyon is also jarring and should STAY hard — a fire-and-ice border is a landmark. Cost is one lerp in the terrain vertex-colour pass; no new data, pass, draw calls or triangles. Sequence after LVL-1, since blending snow into the swamp end interacts with the snow-albedo exposure risk. Full write-up in agents/level-output.md section 8.

openIssues.title: Two donor encounter pairs are closer than one battle staging disc
openIssues.detail: Battle stages in place on a disc of radius R_STAGE = 5.5 m (11.0 m across, derived in docs/specs/heightfields.mjs). frost_canyon e19(40,22) <-> e31(38,26) are 8.9 m apart and last_crown e8(42,25) <-> e34(40,26) are 4.5 m apart, so triggering one stages the fight on top of the other. Verified against games/chronoforge/src/world.js. Both resolved by the Phase 1.3 moves; MIN_ENCOUNTER_SEP_TILES = 6 (12 m) now gates it in world-graph.mjs selfCheck.

openIssues.title: BATTLE_PUSH_IN = 1.20 authored by level because combat clearance could not be derived without it
openIssues.detail: No push-in number existed anywhere. Clearance depends on it, so the two are one decision: the staging disc is 11.0 m across and good framing puts the subject at ~60% of the frame's short dimension, giving a pushed-in ground depth of 18.3 m against the overworld's 22.0 m -> push-in 1.20, battle frame 15.0 m. It lives in docs/specs/heightfields.mjs. `battle` should adopt it in Phase 7 or tell level it changed — a harder push-in tightens clearance and moves some of the 36 placements again.

openIssues.title: Four inherited encounters break tier coherence; e13 is the one that matters
openIssues.detail: Rule: |enemy tier - region tier| <= 1, T5 exempt as elites. Reported, NOT retuned — enemy assignment is gamedesign's and the donor's lane. Named in world-graph.mjs TIER_EXCEPTIONS so a NEW mismatch fails the gate. (1) e13 mire_warden T4 in Mire Bog T2, +2 — the worst: Mire Bog is inside the Survivor starting web, so a level-5 party meets a 165 HP T4 enemy, and it is the ONLY pre-Ascendant source of void_scepter (20% drop), so swapping it moves item pacing. (2) e19 frost_colossus T5 in Frost Canyon T3, +2 — reads as a deliberate superboss, one of two titan_shard sources. (3) e35 gravbot T2 in Crater Ember T4, -2. (4) e33 gravbot T2 in Last Crown T4, -2. The last two are cosmetic; e13 needs a decision.

openIssues.title: Combat clearance derived and all 36 encounters + 8 world drops re-placed against it
openIssues.detail: GAME_PLAN named combat clearance as the constraint on every placement and no number for it existed. Derived from battle staging in docs/specs/heightfields.mjs: R_STAGE 5.5 m (actor geometry, does NOT move with FRAME_HEIGHT_M) with spread <= 1.5*HERO_M = 2.58 m and slope <= 16 deg; R_FRAME 9.16 m (a camera formula over FRAME_HEIGHT_M, so it DOES move — P0-6) with spread <= 6.0 m, from the occlusion threshold d/tan(55 deg). The coupling is asserted: the staging disc must stay under 70% of the pushed-in frame's short dimension, which breaks below FRAME_HEIGHT_M 15.4. 12 of 36 inherited encounters failed; all 36 now pass. 15 encounters moved (4-16 m) and all 8 world drops moved (3-49 m). Stageable fraction per map ranges 100% (Haventide) to 21% (Crater Ember), which puts Crater Ember's fights in its crater floors. World-drop siting rule: >= 20 m from every encounter, >= 12 m from every doorway-to-doorway and doorway-to-city through-route, on dry readable ground, minimum move from the donor tile otherwise.

openIssues.title: The pixel-snap is a no-op at the shipping framing, and pulling the camera in cannot fix it
openIssues.detail: At FRAME_HEIGHT_M 18 the hero measures 43.1 px, so snapUnitPx = 43.1/(1.72*28) = 0.895 — snapping to under one pixel does nothing. The rig spec assumed ~62 px and snapUnitPx 1.3. Framing is NOT the lever: measured, heroPx goes 43.1 -> 47.2 -> 52.1 -> 53.9 as FRAME_HEIGHT_M goes 18 -> 15.4 -> 12.4 -> 11.0, because a vertical character at 55 deg pitch does not scale with metres-of-ground-plane. 62 px is unreachable through the camera, and 15.4 is already the floor Phase 1.3 derived for battle staging. The only lever that reaches the spec is SPRITE_PX_PER_METRE: 19.3 gives snapUnit 1.3, 16.7 gives 1.5, 12.5 gives 2.0 — i.e. a hero of 33 virtual rows rather than 48. Chunkier sprite. ART CALL, not dev.
openIssues.repro: node tools/rig.mjs, then read docs/STATUS.json rig.framing; or open ?dev=1&showcase=actors and read the rig readout

openIssues.title: uPivot 0.34 is calibrated for the gate rig, not for dawn — the cast crushes to black in-world
openIssues.detail: The toon ramp pivots on a linear luminance of 0.34, which suits the measurement gate's own 3.1-intensity key light. Under the game exposure at dawn 6.4 every torso, arm and leg lands in the bottom band: vex resolves to 5 distinct quantised colours over her whole body against kaida's 11. At uPivot 0.10 the palettes come back — kaida reads blue, rune red/gold, the grunt brown. It is a knob, not a structural failure, but the right default needs a sweep across the hour range, not a single dawn frame.
openIssues.repro: node tools/shot.mjs --shots actors-lineup --params showcase=actors --js "__DAWN__.ctx.actors.uniforms.uPivot.value=0.10" — compare shots/phase2/actors-lineup.png against shots/phase2/pivot0.10/

openIssues.title: Actors cast nothing and touch nothing
openIssues.detail: NOT A DEFECT. Verified at noon on flat ground: the actor casts a real shadow and always did — castShadow true, skinned depth material working, 4096 map. At dawn the sun is at 11.6deg and throws it ~4.9m sideways, outside every crop taken. Artifact: shots/ground/noon-shadow.png

openIssues.title: Dither on the actor material reads as checkerboard noise on small limbs
openIssues.detail: MeshStandardMaterial dithering:true plus the snap puts a visible checkerboard on kaida's shins and boots and vex's forearm at review distance. Dither exists to hide banding in a smooth gradient; this material deliberately bands, so the two fight. Try dithering:false.

openIssues.title: docs/specs/rig.mjs prose says the bind pose faces -Z; its own socket offsets say +Z
openIssues.detail: socket.chest sits at z +0.10 and socket.back at z -0.06, which only describes a character facing +Z. src/actors/rig.js builds facing +Z because the offsets are the load-bearing half. Art should correct the prose so the next reader does not trust the wrong half.

openIssues.title: heroScreenPx / snapUnitPx stop updating while a named shot is set
openIssues.detail: updateSnap() runs inside the actors tick, and setShot() pauses the sim, so report() returns the last live value rather than the shot camera's. Harmless for the gate (which never reads it) but it will mislead anyone measuring framing from a capture.

openIssues.title: She stands world-vertical on every slope and both feet sit at one height
openIssues.detail: Placement is a single heightAt() sample at the root, so on a slope the downhill foot floats and the uphill foot buries. At a run her feet are ~0.7 m apart fore-aft; at MAX_WALKABLE_SLOPE_DEG 34 that is 0.47 m of height difference against an 0.88 m leg — more than half a leg in the air. At a routine 20 deg biome slope it is still 0.25 m. Driving the play sample reaches 38 deg on the placeholder dunes. Fix is a stack: slope-align the root 40-60 percent toward the terrain normal (world.normalAt already exists), two-bone foot IK per foot, torso lean by slope, stride shortening uphill. Rigid skinning makes the IK crease correct rather than wrong, and clips write absolute rotations so IK layers after sampling without touching poses.js. RESOLVED 2026-09-04 in src/actors/ground.js; gate is tools/ground.mjs. Planted-foot p95 0.048m -> 0.004m and, more importantly, flat against slope.
openIssues.repro: ?dev=1 then run up a dune and watch the Slope readout; shots/play/run-a.png at 38.3 deg

openIssues.title: A lane cannot collapse or hide another lane's dev-panel group
openIssues.detail: main.js registers time/camera/sim/perf/quality itself and dev.register offers no way to mark a group collapsed, so ?dev=2 look mode hides them by setting display on the .grp divs from src/traversal/index.js. A stopgap in the wrong file. Real fix is a `collapsed` option on dev.register, which is INTEGRATOR ONLY territory. Two related traps found the hard way and worth fixing at the same time: devpanel update() starts `if (root.className) return`, so adding any class to #dawn-dev silently stops its own readouts; and toggles sync() on click only, never per frame, so a toggle misreports state a module changes on its own.

openIssues.title: Hand sockets point every weapon back at its owner's shoulder
openIssues.detail: docs/specs/rig.mjs says a socket's local +Y runs along the prop's extend axis and every weapon is authored grip-at-origin +Y-to-tip. But a hand bone's local +Y points UP the arm toward the elbow, so an unrotated hand socket aims the blade at the shoulder. Kaida's sword hung point-up along her forearm. Fixed by rotating the hand sockets pi about X, but SCOPED TO KAIDA: applying it to everyone failed vex, whose staff is long enough that hanging it correctly puts the tip below her feet and inflates her bind silhouette to 1.816m against a 1.660m spec (9.4% on a 6% band). Two follow-ups: weapons need a per-weapon carry pose (a staff is shouldered or planted, not hung), and the gate's height assertion should measure the body rather than the body plus whatever it holds.
openIssues.repro: remove the B.lofted guard in src/actors/rig.js socket loop, then node tools/rig.mjs

openIssues.title: The pixel-snap grid scaled with camera distance and shattered the character when inspected
openIssues.detail: snapUnitPx is derived from the actor's on-screen height, which is correct at the shipping framing (~0.9px) and catastrophic in ?dev=2 look mode, where it reached 16.6px and broke the character into loose plates with visible gaps. The human read that as a modelling failure; it was the snap. Clamped at SNAP_MAX_PX = 2.4 in src/actors/index.js. Worth revisiting when SPRITE_PX_PER_METRE is finally decided — the clamp and that constant are the same conversation.
openIssues.repro: ?dev=2, zoom in, watch the Rig readout snap value

openIssues.title: tools/rig.mjs --selftest now MISSES the flipped-normals fault
openIssues.detail: Nothing regressed in the rig. The joint-overlap geometry changed the palette histogram enough that a full normal flip no longer clears the tv <= 0.28 band. The tool header flagged PALETTE as the tightest of its four assertions when it was written (2.2x between the worst legitimate pose and a real fault). DO NOT widen the band to make it green — that deletes the assertion. Re-survey clean tv across all four characters and tighten the band to ~1.4x above the new clean worst, the way the originals were derived. UPDATE 2026-09-05: removing the outline hull restored normals-flipped detection — the hull was masking it. --selftest now misses only limb blow-up, which is a silhouette-band miss rather than a palette one.

openIssues.title: Player-chosen camera distance, third-person follow, and per-state LOD
openIssues.detail: Human request, deferred by agreement. Let the player pick camera level at any time: behind-the-shoulder rotating with her, or zoomed out to watch her cross the level from the locked angle. Note this DISSOLVES the SPRITE_PX_PER_METRE question rather than answering it — if the player picks the zoom, no single sprite density was ever right, and the honest design is a per-camera-state LOD that drops sub-pixel work at distance.

openIssues.title: Limb shells rotate apart at every joint and leave visible gaps
openIssues.detail: Rigid skinning weights every vertex 100% to one bone, so nothing deforms and a bend separates the two shells. The OVER=0.045 overlap in kaida.js does NOT fix it and cannot: running each segment past its joint fills the INSIDE of a bend while the outside still opens, because the extension rotates away with its own bone. Fix is a joint sphere at the pivot, parented to one bone, radius = limb radius x 1.05 — every point on both end rings sits exactly the limb radius from the joint centre, so it covers any bend angle permanently. One per shoulder, elbow, hip, knee, ~10 lines. NOT IMPLEMENTED. Moot if the mesh-source decision goes to a smooth-skinned model.
openIssues.repro: ?dev=2, orbit to a three-quarter view and watch the shoulders and knees

openIssues.title: Lava channel reads as a painted ribbon, not a fissure
openIssues.detail: crater_ember lavaChannel is vertex colour on an undeformed surface, on a polyline route INFERRED through craterCentres because the spec gives width/depth/colour but no path. Reads as a glowing hose lying on the ground with hard-cut ends. A real 1.2 m carve over 3.5 m is a 28 deg wall on a biome already at 32 deg and would breach the 34 deg ceiling — so the spec needs a route AND a shoulder width, not just a deeper carve.

openIssues.title: Bog water plane reads as black holes and spills past the map rect
openIssues.detail: mire_bog pools read as voids punched through the ground rather than standing water, worse at noon than dawn. The plane also extends beyond the terrain edge — extra shapes visible off the east edge in the map shot. Needs clipping to the map rect and a real water treatment.

openIssues.title: Authored biome palettes only separate at noon
openIssues.detail: At DAWN_HOUR 6.4 the warm low key multiplies every albedo toward sand — mire_bog (#5f6444 green) and frost_canyon (#9fabb4 grey-blue) both read peach-tan. At 12.5 they read as authored. Biome identity cannot be judged on a dawn capture. Exposure is render/, frozen this session.
openIssues.repro: compare shots at --t 6.4 and --t 12.5 on mire_bog_region

openIssues.title: orbital_reach and crater_ember sit outside the healthy dawn band
openIssues.detail: orbital_reach med 0.396 (snow, washed out), crater_ember med 0.065 (basalt, dark). Both albedos are inside the spec ALBEDO_BAND and p90 <= 0.51 with 0.00% white. Exposure fix belongs to 4b.

openIssues.title: Ground detail normal reads as melted-plastic blobs on mid-tone biomes
openIssues.detail: Most visible on haventide and mire_bog, invisible on frozen_ruins where the albedo is bright. Tiling density was fixed in 4a by scaling UVs against a 240 m reference; the pattern itself is the remaining half. Related to P0-3.

openIssues.title: probe.mjs parses --params but never forwards it to boot()
openIssues.detail: node tools/probe.mjs --params "map=X" silently measures proto instead of X. shot.mjs --probe does forward it and is the working path. One-line fix.

openIssues.title: size = max(w,d) lets traversal walk off the short axis
openIssues.detail: The clamp is size*0.5-4 = +/-41 m on a 60 m-deep map. field.heightAt clamps to the edge value so the player stands on ground rather than falling, but the clamp lives in src/traversal/ and needs the real per-axis extents.

openIssues.title: Every biome under-delivers its own targetReliefM by 12-22%
openIssues.detail: grassland 4.4/5, neon 5.4/6.5, forest 4.2/5, mire 2.7/3.2, frozen 5.6/7, frost_canyon 8.6/11, alien 5.3/6.5, crater 8.4/9.5. Systematic across all eight, so it is one normalisation, not eight authoring calls. frost_canyon is 2.4 m short of the relief that makes its trench read as a canyon.

openIssues.title: Four city-interior exits had never been slope-checked

openIssues.title: 17 of 36 encounter discs overhang the map rect
openIssues.detail: The runtime clamps outside [0,w]x[0,d]; heightfields.heightAt evaluates noise anywhere.
